question: Node.js runs JavaScript on one thread. How can two gates in the same process still race for the last parking spot?
answer_hinglish:
Haan, Node single-threaded hai, lekin single-threaded ka matlab 'no interleaving' nahi hai. Matlab sirf itna hai ki ek SYNCHRONOUS block ke beech mein koi aur code nahi chalta. Jaise hi code `await` karta hai, function wahan ruk jaata hai aur event loop doosre kaam chala deta hai -- doosre gate ka `enter()` bhi.

Ab naive gate socho: pehle check karo 'koi spot free hai?', phir `await` printer (ticket print + barrier), phir park karo. Gate 1 check karta hai -- haan, ek spot free. Printer pe await. Event loop ab Gate 2 chalata hai -- uska check bhi pass, kyunki Gate 1 ne abhi kuch liya hi nahi. Dono printers chal rahe hain, dono barriers khulte hain, aur baad mein doosri `park()` LOT_FULL deti hai -- lekin car toh andar aa chuki hai, bina spot ke.

Toh race thread se nahi, check aur act ke beech ke `await` se aati hai. Rule simple hai: jo check aur jo state change usse guard hota hai, dono ek hi synchronous block mein hone chahiye. Is project mein `ParkingLot` ka har public method synchronous hai -- `reserve()` check bhi karta hai aur spot ko `reserved` bhi kar deta hai, beech mein koi await nahi. Slow device ka kaam gate do lot calls ke BEECH mein karta hai, ek claim pakad ke. Yeh check-then-act race ka classic example hai, bas threads ki jagah async callbacks.
why_needed: Interview mein log aksar kehte hain 'Node mein race condition hoti hi nahi'. Yeh galat hai, aur yeh project usko test se prove karta hai. Yeh samajh har async backend (DB call, HTTP call ke beech) mein kaam aati hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi receptionist (single thread) do customers ko dekh rahi hai. Customer A poochta hai 'room khaali hai?' -- haan. Woh payment ke liye phone uthata hai (await). Tab tak receptionist customer B ko bhi 'haan khaali hai' bol deti hai. Ek receptionist, phir bhi double booking.
how_it_works: Event loop ek time pe ek callback/microtask chalata hai. `await` function ko suspend karta hai aur baaki ka kaam ek promise continuation ban jaata hai. Us beech mein event loop doosre continuations chala sakta hai. Isliye `check; await x; act` mein check aur act do alag 'turns' mein hote hain, aur beech mein koi bhi state badal sakta hai.
in_this_project: `src/parking-lot.ts` ka class comment khud yahi kehta hai: har public method synchronous hai aur 'no other code can run between a check and the change it guards'. `test/gates.test.ts` mein `NaiveEntryGate` -- `availability()` se check, `await this.device.issue(...)`, phir `lot.park()` -- yeh bug reproduce karta hai: test 'two naive entry gates, one free spot' mein `device.calls` ki length 2 hoti hai, yaani do ticket print hue ek spot ke liye.
advantages: Synchronous block ke andar atomicity free mein milti hai, koi lock library nahi chahiye
Race ek deterministic test se reproduce hoti hai, kyunki interleaving test control karta hai
disadvantages: Guarantee sirf ek process ke andar hai
Koi future developer lot method ke andar await daal de toh guarantee chupchaap toot jaati hai
common_mistakes: 'Node single-threaded hai toh race nahi hogi' maan lena
Check ek function mein aur act await ke baad doosre mein karna
Sochna ki race sirf multi-threaded code ka problem hai

Worker threads use karo toh yeh reasoning bachegi?
Yeh race multiple Node processes mein kaise dikhegi?

question: Walk me through the test that reproduces two barriers opening for one spot. How does the test control the interleaving?
answer_hinglish:
Test hai `test/gates.test.ts` mein 'two naive entry gates, one free spot: both barriers open, the second car has no spot'. Lot mein sirf ek compact spot hai. Do `NaiveEntryGate` ek hi `FakeDevice` share karte hain. `g1.enter("A1")` aur `g2.enter("A2")` dono call hote hain bina await kiye, phir `await flush()`.

Trick `FakeDevice` mein hai: uska `issue()` ek promise return karta hai jo khud resolve nahi hota -- woh `calls` array mein `resolve`/`reject` ke saath push ho jaata hai. Matlab device tab tak 'chalta' rehta hai jab tak test khud usko settle na kare. Isse test interleaving decide karta hai, timing pe depend nahi karta -- koi `setTimeout` ya sleep nahi, isliye test flaky nahi hai.

`flush()` ek `setImmediate` ka promise hai, jo pending microtasks ko chalne deta hai. Uske baad assertion: `device.calls` ki length 2 -- dono checks pass hue, do ticket print hue. Phir dono calls resolve hote hain, `Promise.allSettled` se result: pehla fulfilled, doosra rejected with LOT_FULL -- lekin comment kehta hai '...after its barrier opened'. Matlab physical duniya mein car andar aa gayi, aur lot ke paas uske liye spot nahi.

Real `EntryGate` wala test same setup use karta hai aur ulta prove karta hai: p2 turant LOT_FULL se reject hota hai aur `device.calls` ki length 1 hai -- doosre gate ka printer kabhi chala hi nahi.
why_needed: Concurrency bug ko 'kabhi kabhi hota hai' se 'har baar hota hai' banana hi usko fix karne ka pehla step hai. Controllable fake device yeh deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek referee jo do runners ko bolta hai 'ruko', aur khud decide karta hai kaun pehle line cross karega -- race ka result luck pe nahi, referee pe depend karta hai.
how_it_works: Pending promise pattern: `new Promise((resolve, reject) => this.calls.push({ resolve, reject, ... }))`. Test baad mein `calls[i].resolve()` ya `.reject(err)` karta hai. `setImmediate` macrotask queue mein jaata hai, isliye usse pehle saare queued microtasks (await continuations) chal jaate hain.
in_this_project: `FakeDevice` dono `EntryDevice` aur `ExitDevice` implement karta hai. Naive gates test file mein hi likhe hain, library ka hissa nahi hain (README bhi yahi kehta hai). README ke hisaab se `gates.test.ts` mein 12 tests hain, jinme se 2 naive race wale hain.

Bug aur fix dono same setup se dikhte hain, comparison saaf hai
disadvantages: Fake device real hardware ki timing nahi dikhata
Naive gates sirf test mein hain, toh unka code drift ho sakta hai
common_mistakes: Race test mein random `setTimeout` delays use karna (flaky test)
Sirf final state check karna aur `device.calls` count bhool jaana -- bug physical side effect mein hai
allSettled ki jagah `await p2` karke unhandled rejection paana
follow_up_questions: `flush()` ki jagah `await Promise.resolve()` kaafi hoga kya?
Is test ko real `EntryGate` ke against chalao toh kya assert karoge?
Device fake karna aur lot real rakhna -- yeh choice kyun?

question: A customer photocopies their ticket and two cars try to leave at two exits at once. What happens with the naive exit gate, and how does the real ExitGate stop it?
answer_hinglish:
Naive exit gate teen kaam karta hai: `lot.quote(ticketId)` se 'ticket valid hai?' check, phir `await device.open(...)` (barrier), phir `lot.exit(ticketId)`. Copy wale do tickets do exits par aaye: dono ka `quote` pass, dono barriers khulte hain, aur sirf baad mein doosri `exit()` fail hoti hai. Test 'one ticket at two naive exit gates: both barriers open' mein `device.calls` ki length 2 hai -- matlab ek ticket par do gaadiyan bahar.

Real `ExitGate.leave` pehle `lot.beginExit(ticketId)` call karta hai. Yeh synchronous hai: ticket check karta hai, bill fix karta hai, aur ticket ka status `active` se `exiting` kar deta hai -- sab ek block mein. Doosra gate jab `beginExit` call karta hai, `unlocked()` guard dekhta hai status `active` nahi hai aur TICKET_BUSY phenkta hai, barrier chhune se pehle. Test 'one ticket at two exit gates: one barrier opens, the other gets TICKET_BUSY' mein `device.calls` ki length 1 hai aur gateway ne sirf 5000 charge kiya.

Phir device ka kaam ho jaata hai toh `commitExit` spot free karta hai aur ticket bhool jaata hai. Agar device fail ho, `abortExit` status wapas `active` kar deta hai -- car andar hai, ticket phir kaam karega. Point yeh hai ki lock ka owner sirf woh gate hai jisne `beginExit` jeeta, aur yeh jeetna atomic hai kyunki ek synchronous call ke andar hua.
why_needed: Exit par race ka matlab paisa aur security dono: ek ticket par do gaadi nikal sakti hain. Entry race se zyada nuksaan wala bug hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank locker: chaabi ki copy le kar do log do counters par jaate hain. Agar counter pehle register mein 'locker in use' likh deta hai tabhi andar bhejta hai, toh doosre counter ko turant 'busy' dikhega.
how_it_works: `beginExit` -> `unlocked()` (status `active` hona chahiye, warna TICKET_BUSY) -> `bill()` -> `spotOf()` check -> `lockEntry(entry, "exiting", ...)`. Lock mein `at`, `feeMinor`, `paidMinor`, `dueMinor`, `paymentKey` fix ho jaate hain. `commitExit`/`abortExit` dono `exiting()` guard use karte hain.
in_this_project: `src/gates.ts` `ExitGate.leave`, `src/parking-lot.ts` `beginExit`, `unlocked`, `lockEntry`. Do tests: naive wala aur real wala, dono `test/gates.test.ts` mein. `two-phase.test.ts` bhi check karta hai ki exiting ticket par `beginExit` aur `exit` dono TICKET_BUSY dete hain.
advantages: Copy ticket ko barrier se pehle hi refuse karta hai
Fee bhi lock ke time fix ho jaata hai, slow barrier price nahi badalta
Abort par ticket wapas usable
disadvantages: Lock ki koi expiry nahi -- ek gate process mar jaaye toh ticket `exiting` mein atak sakta hai (in-memory hai, process ke saath sab jaata hai)
Copy ticket ko pehchanta nahi, sirf 'pehla aaya pehla gaya'
common_mistakes: Validity check (`quote`) ko lock samajh lena
Gate mein boolean flag rakhna -- har gate ka apna flag hota hai, shared nahi
Device fail hone par lock release karna bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: Agar copy wala pehle pahunch jaaye toh asli owner ka kya?
TICKET_BUSY aur TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE mein farak kya hai?
Pay station aur exit gate same ticket par ek saath aayein toh?

question: Why did you use synchronous claims (reserve/confirm/cancel) instead of putting a mutex around the whole gate operation?
answer_hinglish:
Mutex bhi bug fix kar deta, lekin galat cheez ko serialize karta. Agar poore `enter()` ke around ek lock ho -- check, printer ka await, park -- toh ek time pe sirf ek gate kuch kar sakta. Printer slow hai ya jam hai (default timeout 10 s), toh baaki saare gates uske peeche line mein khade rahenge, chaahe unke liye alag spots free hon. Ek slow printer poore lot ka throughput le doobta.

Claim approach mein lock sirf usi resource par hai jo sach mein contend ho raha hai: ek spot aur ek plate. `reserve()` synchronous hai, spot ko `reserved` kar deta hai aur plate ko `ticketIdByPlate` mein daal deta hai. Uske baad gate bina kisi global lock ke apna slow device chalata hai. Doosra gate turant `reserve()` call kar sakta hai -- usko doosra spot mil jaayega, ya LOT_FULL/ALREADY_PARKED turant, printer chalne se pehle. Kaam khatam: `confirm()`; fail ya timeout: `cancel()`.

Teesra reason: JavaScript mein mutex khud ek promise-queue hota hai jo hume likhna padta, aur woh deadlock/forgotten-release jaisi nayi bugs laata. Yahan atomicity language se free mein milti hai -- synchronous block beech mein interrupt nahi hota. PLAN.md ki decision bhi yahi hai: mutex 'would serialise every gate behind the slowest printer', aur 'check, await, act' khud bug hai.

Trade-off: claim ka state explicit model karna pada -- spot ka teesra state `reserved`, ticket ke statuses `reserved`/`exiting`, aur har failure path par rollback. Yeh zyada code hai, lekin har cheez test ho sakti hai.
why_needed: Concurrency design ka asli sawaal 'lock lagana hai ya nahi' nahi, 'kis cheez par aur kitni der' hai. Interviewer yahi granularity samajh dekhna chahta hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein ek hi darwaza (mutex) jahan har group ko table milne tak andar ka poora process -- order, khana -- khatam hone ka wait karna pade, vs host jo turant table par 'reserved' card rakh deta hai aur agle group ko doosri table de deta hai.
how_it_works: Claim = state machine ka ek intermediate state jo synchronously set hota hai. Slow kaam claim ke andar hota hai, bahar nahi. Har exit path claim ko terminal state mein le jaata hai: confirm/commitExit (success) ya cancel/abortExit (rollback). Doosre actors claim dekh ke turant fail-fast karte hain.
in_this_project: `EntryGate.enter`: `lot.reserve()` -> `await withTimeout(device.issue)` -> `lot.confirm()`, catch mein `lot.cancel()`. `ExitGate.leave`: `beginExit` -> payment/device -> `commitExit`, catch mein `abortExit`. Test 'while the device runs, the spot is reserved, not free and not parked' state ko device ke beech mein check karta hai.
advantages: Gates parallel chalte hain; sirf same spot/plate par contention
Fail-fast: doosre gate ka device chalta hi nahi
Koi lock library, deadlock ya forgotten release nahi
disadvantages: Explicit intermediate states aur har path par rollback likhna padta hai
Claim ki koi expiry nahi (crashed gate ka reservation kabhi clear nahi hota)
common_mistakes: Mutex ko poore async operation ke around lagana
Claim lena lekin catch mein rollback bhool jaana
Sochna ki claim aur mutex mein farak sirf naam ka hai
follow_up_questions: Agar ek hi spot wala lot ho toh claim aur mutex mein farak bachega?
Claim crash-safe kaise banaoge?
Per-spot mutex vs claim -- kya farak hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Mutex: kam states, simple code, lekin throughput sabse slow device tak gir jaata hai. Claim: zyada states aur rollback code, lekin contention sirf usi spot/plate par. Is lot ke liye claim behtar kyunki gates ka slow kaam (printer, barrier, payment) independent hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Claim leke gate crash: spot aur plate hamesha ke liye atke (README ka known gap, expiry sweep nahi bana). Mutex ke saath bhi crash ho toh lock atak sakta tha -- dono ko lease/timeout chahiye. Device hang ko `withTimeout` cover karta hai, crash ko nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Per-spot mutex (zyada complex, same result); optimistic concurrency (version number check at confirm); queue-based single writer jo saare gate requests serially process kare -- yahan lot ke synchronous methods effectively wahi single writer hain.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x gates ek process mein: claim approach bina change ke scale karta hai kyunki critical section microseconds ka hai. 100x aur multiple processes: claim ko database mein le jaana padega (conditional UPDATE / unique constraint) -- README ke hisaab se yeh built nahi hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Claim mein `claimedAt` aur ek expiry sweep, gate ki heartbeat, metrics: active reservations count aur unki age, aur alert jab koi reservation gate timeout se kaafi purana ho.

question: Your claim is safe inside one Node process. What breaks if you run three gate processes against a shared database, and how would you move the claim there?
answer_hinglish:
Ek process mein safety is baat par tiki hai ki `reserve()` ka check aur change ek synchronous block hai, aur saara state usi process ki memory mein hai. Teen processes ka matlab teen alag memories: har ek ke paas apna `ParkingLot` hai, toh unke liye shared state hai hi nahi. Agar state database mein le jaayein lekin code wahi rahe -- SELECT free spot, phir UPDATE -- toh SELECT aur UPDATE ke beech network round trip hai, aur doosra process wahi spot select kar sakta hai. Wahi check-then-act race wapas, bas await ki jagah network.

Fix ka idea same hai, bas claim wahan jaata hai jahan state rehta hai -- README ke shabdon mein 'the same idea, moved to where the state lives'. Spot ke liye conditional UPDATE: `UPDATE spots SET state='reserved', held_by=$t WHERE id=$s AND state='free'`. Database row lock ke saath yeh atomic hai; affected rows 0 aaye toh kisi aur ne jeet liya, agla spot try karo. Plate ke liye unique constraint (ek plate ka ek hi open ticket), toh ALREADY_PARKED database enforce karega. Exit lock: `UPDATE tickets SET status='exiting' WHERE id=$t AND status='active'` -- 0 rows matlab TICKET_BUSY.

Imaandari se: is project mein yeh implement nahi hai. Sab in-memory, ek Node process. Aur multi-process mein ek nayi problem aati hai jo ek process mein chhupi hai: process crash. Ek process mein crash ho toh saari memory ke saath reservation bhi chala jaata hai; database mein reservation reh jaayega. Toh lease (`reserved_at` + expiry sweep) wahan zaroori ho jaata hai.
why_needed: Real parking systems (aur koi bhi booking system -- seats, inventory) multiple servers par chalte hain. Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki tum single-process trick ko distributed version mein translate kar sakte ho ya nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ek hall ke andar ek hi register (ek process) -- koi bhi pen uthaaye, ek time pe ek hi likhta hai. Teen buildings mein teen registers ho jaayein toh har building apni 'khaali seat' bata degi. Solution: ek central register jisme likhne ka rule hai 'sirf tab likho jab line abhi blank ho'.
how_it_works: Atomicity ka source badal jaata hai: event loop ke synchronous block ki jagah database ka single-statement atomicity aur row locks / unique index. Pattern compare-and-set hai: 'state X se Y karo sirf agar abhi X hai', result count se pata chalta hai jeete ya nahi. Slow device ka kaam ab bhi claim ke bahar, do DB statements ke beech.
in_this_project: Code mein jo concepts DB mein jaayenge: `ParkingSpot.reserve` ka guard (`current !== "free"` -> SPOT_STATE), `ticketIdByPlate` map (unique plate), `unlocked()` ka TICKET_BUSY. README ki 'Concurrency' section aur PLAN.md ki stage 2 decision dono clearly likhte hain 'Not built'.
code_example:
-- illustrative, NOT in the repo: the same claims as database statements
UPDATE spots SET state = 'reserved', held_by = $ticket, reserved_at = now()
 WHERE id = $spot AND state = 'free';          -- 0 rows: someone else won, try the next spot

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_open_ticket_per_plate ON tickets (plate) WHERE closed_at IS NULL;  -- ALREADY_PARKED

UPDATE tickets SET status = 'exiting', exit_at = now()
 WHERE id = $ticket AND status = 'active';     -- 0 rows: TICKET_BUSY
advantages: Same mental model: claim, slow work, confirm or rollback
Database atomicity sab processes ke liye ek hi source of truth
disadvantages: Har claim ek network round trip
Crash ke baad orphan claims ke liye lease/expiry zaroori
Hot spot contention par retries badhte hain
common_mistakes: SELECT-then-UPDATE ko atomic samajhna
Process memory mein cache rakhna aur usse decisions lena
Sochna ki ek bada distributed lock (Redis) hi ek jawab hai
follow_up_questions: Conditional UPDATE vs SELECT ... FOR UPDATE -- kab kya?
Orphan reservations ko kaun aur kab saaf karega?
Agar database region-wise replicated ho toh?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Conditional UPDATE: lock sirf ek row par, chhota; SELECT FOR UPDATE: transaction lamba hota hai aur agar uske andar device ka wait kiya toh wahi 'mutex around the gate' problem. Distributed lock (Redis): ek aur system, aur lock expire hone ke baad bhi purana holder likh sakta hai bina fencing token ke.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Process reserve karke mar gaya: row `reserved` mein atki -- lease expiry chahiye. DB down: koi gate entry nahi de sakta (fail closed) ya offline mode chahiye. Network timeout UPDATE ke baad: pata nahi claim hua ya nahi -- idempotent ticket id se retry.
advanced.alternatives: Single writer service (saare gates ek lot-service ko call karein, jo in-memory claims rakhe) -- yeh is project ka model hi hai, bas network ke peeche; sharding per lot taaki har lot ka ek owner ho; optimistic version column.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: ek DB, row-level contention sirf last spots par; index on (lot, size, state). 100x lots: lot_id se shard, kyunki claims kabhi lots ke beech cross nahi karte.
advanced.production_improvements: reserved_at par expiry sweep, gate heartbeat, metric 'claims older than gate timeout', aur idempotent API taaki network retry double reservation na banaye.

question: The same car (same plate, typed differently) arrives at two entry gates at the same time. What stops it from getting two tickets?
answer_hinglish:
`reserve()` sirf spot claim nahi karta, plate bhi claim karta hai. Pehle `normalizePlate` plate ko upper-case karta hai aur spaces aur '-' hata deta hai -- `mh 12 ab 1234` aur `MH12AB1234` ek hi string ban jaate hain. Phir check: `ticketIdByPlate.has(plate)` -- agar hai toh ALREADY_PARKED. Agar sab checks pass, toh usi synchronous block mein `this.ticketIdByPlate.set(plate, ticket.id)` hota hai.

Important baat: plate map mein reservation ke time hi entry ho jaati hai, confirm ke time nahi. Agar plate sirf `confirm()` par register hoti, toh dono gates ke printers chal rahe hote aur doosra confirm hone par hi pata chalta -- wahi race. README isliye ALREADY_PARKED ko 'that plate is inside or entering at another gate' bolta hai.

Test 'the same plate at two gates at once gets one ticket' do `EntryGate` mein `MH12AB1234` aur `mh 12 ab 1234` bhejta hai. p2 ALREADY_PARKED se reject hota hai, sirf ek device call hota hai, aur end mein `activeTickets` ki length 1 hai. `two-phase.test.ts` bhi check karta hai ki reservation ke dauraan same plate ka doosra `reserve` ALREADY_PARKED deta hai, lekin `findByPlate` reservation ko return nahi karta -- woh sirf parked cars dikhata hai. Aur `cancel()` (via `forget`) plate ko map se hata deta hai, toh device fail hone par wahi car dobara try kar sakti hai.
why_needed: Ek plate do tickets matlab ek car do spots le sakti hai, ya baad mein galat ticket se nikal sakti hai. Plate bhi ek shared resource hai jise claim karna hai, sirf spot nahi.
real_world_analogy: Hotel mein ek hi aadmi do counters par check-in kare. Agar ID number register mein 'check-in in progress' likh diya jaata hai, toh doosra counter turant mana kar dega -- chahe naam alag spelling mein likha ho.
how_it_works: Normalization -> uniqueness check -> claim, teeno ek synchronous method mein. Plate key ka lifecycle: reserve par set, cancel ya commitExit par delete (`forget()`), reportLost par naye ticket id par point.
in_this_project: `src/parking-lot.ts`: `normalizePlate` (PLATE_RE `^[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$`), `reserve` mein ALREADY_PARKED check, `forget` mein `ticketIdByPlate.delete`. Mutation S20 ('findByPlate returns reservations') README mein 1 test se pakda gaya.
advantages: Plate uniqueness entry ke dauraan bhi enforce hoti hai
Normalization se spelling ka farak bypass nahi hota
disadvantages: Crashed gate ka reservation plate ko bhi atka deta hai -- wahi car kisi aur gate se nahi aa sakti
Plate fake ho sakti hai; lot sirf string compare karta hai
common_mistakes: Plate ko sirf confirm par register karna
Normalize kiye bina compare karna
Cancel par plate map se hatana bhool jaana

question: Explain the randomized concurrent-gates test. What does 'every pending device call is backed by a claim' mean and why is that the right invariant?
answer_hinglish:
`test/invariants.test.ts` ka 'random concurrent gates' block 5 seeds (5, 6, 7, 8, 9) par chalta hai. Har run mein 3 `EntryGate` aur 2 `ExitGate` ek lot par, 400 random steps. Har step mein ya toh ek random gate par entry shuru hoti hai, ya ek parked car ka exit, ya ek pending device call random order mein settle hota hai -- 15% chance se `device fault` reject. Exit gates ek fake card reader se pay karte hain jo kabhi approve, kabhi decline, kabhi fail, kabhi charge karke jawab kho deta hai. PRNG seeded (mulberry32) hai, toh failure seed se reproduce hota hai.

Har step ke baad, ek `setImmediate` ke baad, do cheezein check hoti hain. Pehli: `pending` array mein jo bhi device call abhi chal raha hai, uske ticket ka `statusOf` entry ke liye `reserved` aur exit ke liye `exiting` hona chahiye. Yahi 'backed by a claim' hai: koi printer ya barrier tab tak chal hi nahi sakta jab tak lot mein uska claim na ho. Agar koi gate bina claim ke device chalaye (naive gate) ya device ke chalte claim chhod de (rollback bug), yeh line pakad legi. Doosri: `checkInvariants` -- spot states ticket statuses se match, har parked ticket apne fitting spot ko hold kare, koi plate do baar nahi, `DisplayBoard` == `availability()`.

End mein: har failure code allowed list mein ho, provider ka total charged == lot ka total recorded, payment ids unique, har nikli car ne poori fee di, aur device calls ki ginti exactly un operations ke barabar jo claim le paaye. Yeh invariant isliye sahi hai kyunki bug ka asli nuksaan physical side effect hai -- ek printer jo bina spot ke chala.
why_needed: Hand-written concurrency tests sirf woh interleavings check karte hain jo humne socha. Random interleaving aur har step par invariant check un orderings ko pakadta hai jo humne nahi socha.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka auditor jo har transaction ke baad nahi, har second vault aur register dono milata hai -- 'jitne bhi locker khule hain, har ek ka register mein entry hai?'
how_it_works: Model-free property testing: expected output calculate nahi kiya jaata, sirf rules check hote hain jo hamesha sach hone chahiye. Interleaving random hai lekin seed se fixed, toh reproducible. Devices pending promises hain jo test khud settle karta hai.
in_this_project: `invariants.test.ts`: `rng` (mulberry32), `pendingCall`, `checkInvariants`, describe 'random concurrent gates'. Exit device calls `exitCalls++` device ke andar ginte hain, kyunki exit ka device call payment ke await ke baad aata hai, `leave()` ke time nahi. README: invariants file mein total 15 tests.
advantages: Socha na gaya interleaving bhi cover hota hai
Seeded, isliye failure reproducible
Ek hi run mein concurrency, payments aur Observer teeno check

question: The safety of the whole design rests on ParkingLot methods being synchronous. What could quietly break that, and how would you guard against it?
answer_hinglish:
Sabse seedha tareeka: koi lot method ke andar `await` daal de -- jaise pricing ko async bana diya (remote rate service se fee), ya allocation strategy ko async (ek ML model se spot chuno). Tab `reserve()` mein LOT_FULL check aur `spot.reserve()` ke beech ek await aa jaayega aur race wapas. TypeScript isko pakad lega agar interfaces sync hain -- `PricingStrategy.fee` number return karta hai aur `AllocationStrategy.choose` spot return karta hai -- lekin koi interface badal de toh compiler khush rahega.

Doosra subtle raasta: re-entrancy. Lot listeners ko synchronously call karta hai (`changeFree` -> `events.emit`). Agar listener lot ko change kare (jaise valet wala listener), toh woh ek half-done change ke beech mein chal sakta tha. Isliye `changeFree` har method mein LAST call hai ('last: listeners see the finished change'), aur `EventQueue` nested events ko queue karta hai. Mutation S16 ('reserve emits before the spot is taken') README mein 11 tests (stage 2) se pakdi gayi.

Teesra: 'check everything, then change' rule. Agar method beech mein throw kare, toh aadha state badla reh jaata. `reserve()` mein comment hai 'All checks passed; from here on nothing can fail.'

Guard: (1) interfaces synchronous rakho aur unke comment mein reason likho; (2) agar kuch async chahiye (remote pricing), toh usko gate level par, claim ke bahar ya claim ke andar karo, lot ke andar nahi; (3) tests jo before/after poora lot compare karte hain aur random concurrent test -- agar koi await ghus gaya, 'backed by a claim' invariant toot jaayega.
why_needed: Aisi guarantee jo convention par tiki ho, kisi refactor mein chupchaap toot jaati hai. Senior engineer se expect hota hai ki woh batayega guarantee kis assumption par hai aur usse kaise protect karein.
real_world_analogy: Ek operation theatre ka rule: 'surgery ke beech darwaza nahi khulega'. Koi naya nurse beech mein darwaza khol de 'sirf ek second ke liye' -- rule toot gaya. Darwaze par lock aur board dono chahiye.
how_it_works: Atomicity ki boundary = ek synchronous call stack. Boundary ke andar koi await, koi callback jo baad mein chale, ya koi half-applied mutation ke baad throw nahi hona chahiye. Listener callbacks andar chalte hain, isliye unko state change ke BAAD chalana zaroori.
in_this_project: `src/parking-lot.ts` class comment, `reserve` ka 'from here on nothing can fail', `changeFree` aur `forget` mein '// last' comments. `src/events.ts` `EventQueue.emit` queue + `delivering` flag. `checkedFee` pricing ke result ko validate karta hai (STRATEGY_BUG) -- lekin agar pricing Promise return kare toh `Number.isSafeInteger` false hoga aur STRATEGY_BUG aayega, yeh ek accidental safety net hai.
advantages: Atomicity ke liye koi runtime cost nahi
Sync interfaces type system se partially enforce hote hain
disadvantages: Guarantee implicit hai; documentation aur tests par depend
Remote pricing jaisi cheez seedhe plug nahi ho sakti
common_mistakes: Strategy ko async banana 'kyunki sab async hai'
Listener ko state change se pehle call karna
Beech mein throw karne wala validation baad mein daalna
follow_up_questions: Remote pricing service chahiye toh design kaise badloge?
Lint rule se 'no await in ParkingLot' enforce kar sakte ho?
Listener lot ko change kare toh order kaise bachta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Sync core simple aur fast hai lekin har external dependency (rates, ML allocation) ko pehle fetch karke pass karna padta hai -- design caller par bojh daalta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Async pricing: race wapas. Listener throw: EventQueue pakadta hai, change rehta hai. Listener jo lot change kare: queue order bachata hai. Strategy galat spot de: STRATEGY_BUG, lot unchanged.
advanced.alternatives: Lot ke andar ek async mutex (har method serialize) -- lekin tab har call await ho jaayegi aur API async ban jaayega; ya actor model jahan lot ek message queue process kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Ek process mein scale ka issue nahi -- critical section chhota hai. Multi-process mein yeh boundary database transaction ban jaati hai (built nahi).
advanced.production_improvements: ESLint rule (`require-await`/custom rule) ParkingLot file ke liye, interface comments, aur ek test jo asserts kare ki lot ke methods Promise return nahi karte.

question: A spot has three states: free, reserved, occupied. How are the transitions implemented, and why is this not the State pattern?
answer_hinglish:
`src/spot.ts` mein `ParkingSpot` ke paas do private fields hain: `current` (SpotState: `free`/`reserved`/`occupied`) aur `holder` (ticket id ya null). Har transition ek method hai jo pehle guard check karta hai, fail ho toh SPOT_STATE throw:

- `reserve(ticketId)`: sirf `free` se; state `reserved`, holder set.
- `confirm(ticketId)`: sirf `reserved` se aur sirf same holder; state `occupied`.
- `release(ticketId)`: `reserved` ya `occupied` se, sirf holder; state `free`, holder null. Yahi cancel aur exit dono ke liye use hota hai.
- `transfer(from, to)`: lost ticket ke liye, sirf `occupied` aur sirf current holder.

Holder check important hai: koi bug doosre ticket ka spot free nahi kar sakta. Mutation S25 ('spot.confirm does not check the holder') aur S26 ('spot.transfer does not check the holder') isi ke liye the; S26 stage 3 mein survive hua tha kyunki koi galat ticket se transfer call hi nahi karta tha -- naya spot test add hua aur ab pakda jaata hai.

State pattern kyun nahi: State pattern tab useful hai jab har state ka apna behaviour ho -- jaise 'occupied' spot alag tarah se price kare. Yahan kisi state ka apna behaviour nahi hai, sirf 'kaunsa transition allowed hai'. Teen classes (FreeState, ReservedState, OccupiedState) banana sirf indirection hota. PLAN.md: 'Still guarded methods, not the State pattern (no state has behaviour of its own)'.
why_needed: Reserved state hi concurrency fix ka base hai: spot 'na free na occupied' -- printer chal raha hai. Bina iske claim express hi nahi hota.
real_world_analogy: Hotel room ka board: 'Available', 'Held for guest X', 'Occupied by guest X'. Sirf receptionist jiske naam par hold hai, wahi usse 'occupied' kar sakta hai.
how_it_works: String union type + guarded mutator methods. Har method ek precondition check, phir do fields set. Invalid transition exception phenkta hai aur state change nahi hota.
in_this_project: `spot.test.ts` (6 tests): free -> reserved -> occupied -> free, cancel, transfer sirf holder se, aur har refused transition holder ko waise hi chhodta hai. Lot level par `snapshot()` har spot ka `state` aur `heldBy` dikhata hai.
advantages: Chhota, padhne mein seedha
Holder check galat ticket se free hone ko rokta hai
Naya state add karna ek union member + guard hai
disadvantages: States badhe aur behaviour aaya (jaise EV charging) toh refactor karna padega
Transitions ek table mein nahi, methods mein bikhre hain
common_mistakes: Har state ke liye class bana dena bina behaviour ke
Sirf state check karna, holder nahi
Spot ka state aur lot ka ticket status alag-alag drift hone dena
follow_up_questions: Kab State pattern lagana sahi hoga?
Spot state aur ticket status ek hi cheez kyun nahi?
SPOT_STATE error caller tak kab pahunch sakta hai?

question: Walk me through withTimeout. How does it use AbortController, why does it clear the timer, and what happens to a late answer?
answer_hinglish:
`withTimeout(work, timeoutMs)` ek async kaam ko deadline deta hai. Steps:

1. Ek `AbortController` banta hai. Uska `signal` work ko diya jaata hai -- device ya gateway ko.
2. Ek `timeout` promise banta hai jo `setTimeout` ke baad `controller.abort()` karta hai aur reject hota hai ('no answer within N ms').
3. `Promise.race([work, timeout])` -- jo pehle settle ho, wahi result. Work ko `(async () => work(controller.signal))()` mein wrap kiya hai taaki synchronously throw karne wala device bhi normal rejection ban jaaye.
4. `finally { clearTimeout(timer) }` -- har case mein.

Timer clear karna kyun zaroori: fast device ke baad bhi timer pending rahe toh Node process utni der zinda rahega, aur test mein timers leak honge. Test 'a fast device clears its timer (no timer left behind)' fake timers ke saath `vi.getTimerCount()` ko 0 expect karta hai. Mutation S6 isi ko todta hai.

Late answer: timeout ke baad race already reject ho chuka, toh baad mein work ka resolve kisi ke liye matter nahi karta -- race ek hi baar settle hota hai. Gate ne tab tak `cancel()` kar diya hai. Test 'a device that hangs' mein printer timeout ke baad resolve hota hai aur lot ka `snapshot()` bilkul same rehta hai.

Lekin dhyaan: `abort()` promise ko 'kill' nahi karta. JavaScript mein cancellation cooperative hai -- device ko signal dekh ke khud rukna padta hai. README isliye likhta hai ki device ko signal honour karna padega; tests ke fakes karte hain, real hardware project mein nahi hai.
why_needed: Bina timeout ke ek hung printer reservation ko hamesha ke liye pakad ke rakhta. Timeout claim ko time-bound banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Pizza order par 30 minute ka timer: time khatam toh order cancel aur delivery boy ko phone 'mat aana'. Woh phir bhi aa jaaye toh darwaza nahi khulta -- order already cancel.
how_it_works: Promise.race dono promises par handlers attach karta hai, toh haarne wala promise baad mein reject bhi ho toh unhandled rejection nahi. Timer clear ho gaya toh timeout promise kabhi settle nahi hota -- koi problem nahi, woh garbage collect ho jaata hai.
in_this_project: `src/timeout.ts` mein `withTimeout` aur `sleep`. `EntryGate` aur `ExitGate` dono `this.timeoutMs` (default `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`) ke saath use karte hain; `chargeWithRetry` bhi har attempt par timeout lagata hai (README: 'retried up to 3 times with a timeout each').
advantages: Har path par timer clear
Signal se well-behaved device ruk sakta hai
Sync throw bhi rejection ban jaata hai
disadvantages: Cancellation cooperative -- bura device signal ignore kare toh barrier phir bhi khul sakta hai
Timeout error generic `Error` hai; gate usko DEVICE_FAILED ke cause mein wrap karta hai
common_mistakes: `clearTimeout` bhoolna
Sochna ki `abort()` promise ko rok deta hai
Timeout par signal abort na karna (device chalta rahe)

question: How does the lot decide between RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND, TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE, TICKET_BUSY and EXIT_NOT_STARTED? Walk through the guard helpers.
answer_hinglish:
Lot har ticket ke liye ek `Entry` rakhta hai jiska `status` hai: `reserved` | `active` | `paying` | `exiting` (`TicketStatus`). Har public method ek private guard helper se entry nikalta hai, aur wahi helper sahi error code deta hai:

- `reservation(id)`: entry ho aur status `reserved` ho, warna RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND. `confirm` aur `cancel` yahi use karte hain. Parked car ka id, already cancelled id, ya unknown id -- sab RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND.
- `parked(id)`: entry nahi hai aur id `replaced` set mein hai toh TICKET_REPLACED; entry nahi ya status `reserved` toh TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE. Matlab reserve hua lekin car andar nahi aayi, toh us ticket se quote/exit nahi.
- `unlocked(id)`: `parked` + status `active` hona chahiye, warna TICKET_BUSY ('a payment' ya 'an exit' already in progress). `beginExit` aur `beginPayment` use karte hain.
- `exiting(id)`: `parked` + status `exiting`, warna EXIT_NOT_STARTED. `commitExit` aur `abortExit`.

Order matter karta hai: `commitExit("nope")` pehle `parked` se guzarta hai, toh TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE aata hai, EXIT_NOT_STARTED nahi. Test 'commit and abort need a started exit, changing nothing otherwise' yeh dono check karta hai aur poore lot ka before/after JSON compare karta hai.

Fayda: har error ka ek specific matlab hai jo gate UI dikha sakta hai -- 'ticket abhi doosre gate par use ho raha hai' (TICKET_BUSY) vs 'ticket valid nahi' (TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE). Aur guard helpers state change se pehle chalte hain, toh error ka matlab hamesha 'kuch nahi badla'.
why_needed: Concurrency mein error codes hi caller ko batate hain ki retry kare, wait kare ya refuse kare. Generic 'invalid' sab ko ek kar deta.
real_world_analogy: Office ke darwaze par alag boards: 'Appointment nahi mili' (RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND), 'Pass invalid' (TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE), 'Andar meeting chal rahi hai, wait karo' (TICKET_BUSY), 'Pehle reception par sign-in karo' (EXIT_NOT_STARTED).
how_it_works: Guards layered hain: `unlocked` aur `exiting` dono `parked` ko call karte hain, toh common checks ek jagah. Har guard sirf read karta hai; mutation baad mein hoti hai.
in_this_project: `src/parking-lot.ts`: `reservation`, `parked`, `unlocked`, `exiting`, `TicketStatus`. `src/errors.ts` mein har code ke saath ek one-line comment. Mutation S18 ('no TICKET_BUSY check') stage 2 mein 7 aur stage 3 re-run mein 9 tests se pakdi gayi.

Guards reuse hote hain, duplicate checks nahi
Error = kuch nahi badla (before/after tests)
disadvantages: Codes ki list lambi hai (README mein 20+)
Caller ko codes ka order samajhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Ek generic 'INVALID_TICKET' sab ke liye
Guard aur mutation ko mix karna
Reserved ticket ko quote/exit ke liye allow kar dena

Reserved ticket ke liye TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE kyun, RESERVATION alag code kyun nahi?

question: Read EntryGate.enter line by line. What does each line guarantee?
answer_hinglish:
`enter(plate, vehicle)` sirf chaar logical steps hai:

1. `const ticket = this.lot.reserve(plate, vehicle);` -- synchronous claim. Yahan plate normalize, vehicle check, ALREADY_PARKED, LOT_FULL, strategy check sab hota hai. Kuch fail hua toh exception seedha caller ko -- device kabhi chhua hi nahi. Pass hua toh spot `reserved`, plate taken, ticket bana (entry time = abhi).

2. `await withTimeout((signal) => this.device.issue(ticket, signal), this.timeoutMs);` -- slow part: ticket print, barrier open. Claim pakda hua hai, toh doosre gates is spot ko free nahi dekhte. Timeout default 10 s.

3. `catch (cause)` -- device ne reject kiya, sync throw kiya, ya timeout hua: `this.lot.cancel(ticket.id)` spot aur plate free karta hai, phir `DEVICE_FAILED` throw with `{ cause }` taaki asli error (jaise 'paper jam') chhupe nahi.

4. `return this.lot.confirm(ticket.id);` -- success: spot `occupied`, status `active`. Ab car parked hai aur ticket exit ke liye valid.

Dhyaan do ki `confirm` try block ke BAHAR hai. Agar woh andar hota aur kisi wajah se throw karta, toh catch `cancel` chalata aur misleading DEVICE_FAILED deta, jabki device theek tha. `ExitGate.leave` bhi same shape follow karta hai: `beginExit` -> try { payment; device } catch { abortExit } -> `commitExit`.
why_needed: Yeh method poore concurrency design ka chhota sa template hai: claim, slow kaam, confirm ya rollback. Interview mein yahi code whiteboard par likhna padta hai.
real_world_analogy: Cinema ki seat booking: pehle seat 'hold' (reserve), phir payment page (slow), success par 'booked' (confirm), fail par hold chhodo (cancel).
how_it_works: Synchronous claim -> await under claim -> synchronous commit. Rollback sirf us await ke failure ke liye; reserve ka failure kuch claim nahi karta toh rollback ki zaroorat nahi.
in_this_project: `src/gates.ts` `EntryGate` constructor mein `options.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`. Tests: 'device failure: DEVICE_FAILED with the cause...', 'a device that throws synchronously...', 'a device that hangs...', 'while the device runs, the spot is reserved...'.
advantages: Chhota aur review karne mein aasaan
Cause preserve hota hai debugging ke liye
Har failure path par spot wapas
disadvantages: Gate process crash ho toh catch chalta hi nahi -- reservation atka rehta hai
Device ka timeout ke baad barrier kholna lot nahi rok sakta
common_mistakes: confirm ko try ke andar rakhna
Error ko naya bana ke cause kho dena
reserve se pehle device chalana

question: The ticket printer jams while a car is at the entry gate. What exactly happens to the spot, the plate and the error the caller sees?
answer_hinglish:
Printer jam ka matlab `device.issue()` ka promise reject hota hai (test mein `new Error("paper jam")`). `EntryGate.enter` ka catch block chalta hai:

1. `this.lot.cancel(ticket.id)` -- `reservation()` guard pass (status abhi `reserved`), phir `forget()`: spot `release` hokar `free`, `index.released(spot)` se free-spot index mein wapas, entry delete, plate `ticketIdByPlate` se delete, aur `changeFree(+1)` se display board ko event.
2. Caller ko `ParkingError` milta hai code DEVICE_FAILED ke saath, aur `cause` mein original 'paper jam' error.

Test 'device failure: DEVICE_FAILED with the cause, reservation cancelled, spot and plate free again' yeh sab check karta hai: `statusOf(ticketId)` undefined, spot `free`, aur phir same plate `A1` se `lot.park()` ussi spot `L0-1` par chal jaata hai -- matlab plate bhi free hui aur index ne spot wapas diya.

Agar device synchronously throw kare (driver crash), wahi path: `withTimeout` ka async wrapper usko rejection bana deta hai; test 'a device that throws synchronously is handled like a failed one' spot ko `free` expect karta hai.

Ek honest limitation: lot sirf itna jaanta hai ki device ne 'fail' bola. Agar printer ne aadha ticket print kar diya aur barrier khul gaya, toh lot ka record kehta hai car andar nahi hai. Real hardware ka yeh mismatch project ke scope mein nahi hai.
why_needed: Failure par 'kuch nahi bacha' guarantee na ho toh har jam ek spot kha jaata -- lot dheere-dheere 'full' dikhne lagta jabki khaali hai.
real_world_analogy: ATM se paise nahi nikle (machine jam) toh account se debit reverse ho jaata hai aur slip par reason likha hota hai.
how_it_works: Rollback path: gate catch -> lot.cancel -> forget (spot release, index push, entry delete, plate delete, event). Error wrapping ES2022 `Error` `cause` option se.
in_this_project: `src/gates.ts` EntryGate catch, `src/parking-lot.ts` `cancel` aur `forget`, `src/free-index.ts` `released`. Mutation S2 ('entry gate does not cancel on device failure') README mein stage 2 par 3 tests aur stage 3 re-run par 4 tests se pakdi gayi.

Original error cause mein safe
disadvantages: Physical duniya (barrier sach mein khula ya nahi) lot nahi jaanta
Gate crash ho toh catch nahi chalta

Index mein spot wapas na daalna (mutation S9)
Error message mein cause na dena

question: The entry printer hangs forever. Walk through the timeout path, and explain what happens if the printer finally answers after the timeout.
answer_hinglish:
`EntryGate` har device call ko `withTimeout(..., this.timeoutMs)` mein wrap karta hai (default 10 s). Hang ka matlab promise na resolve na reject. Timer fire hota hai: `controller.abort()` -- device ko diya gaya signal aborted ho jaata hai -- aur timeout promise reject. `Promise.race` reject hota hai, gate ka catch `lot.cancel()` karta hai aur DEVICE_FAILED throw.

Test 'a device that hangs' fake timers use karta hai: `timeoutMs: 5000`, 4999 ms advance karo -- spot abhi bhi `reserved` (time se pehle kuch nahi hota). 1 ms aur -- DEVICE_FAILED, `device.calls[0].signal.aborted` true, spot `free`. Phir printer 'finally answers' -- `resolve()` -- aur `snapshot()` ka JSON pehle jaisa hi rehta hai. Late answer kuch nahi badalta kyunki race already settle ho chuka aur gate ka function aage badh chuka; `confirm` kabhi call nahi hota.

Teen cheezein jo yahan galat ho sakti thi, aur README ki mutations unhe test karti hain: S5 -- timeout signal abort na kare (device chalta rahe, barrier baad mein khul sakta); S6 -- fast device ke baad timer clear na ho; S7 -- race hi na ho (hang = gate hamesha ke liye atka, claim kabhi release nahi). Teeno stage 2 par exactly ek test se pakdi gayi.

Sabse important limitation: lot sirf signal abort kar sakta hai; device ko usse respect karna hai. Agar asli barrier driver signal ignore karke timeout ke baad khul jaaye, toh car andar aa jaayegi aur spot already free ho chuka -- wahi original bug. README: 'The device must honour the AbortSignal... real hardware is not part of this project.'
why_needed: Network aur hardware ka sabse common failure 'koi jawab nahi' hota hai, error nahi. Bina timeout ke ek hung device claim ko hamesha pakad ke rakhega.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein waiter ne 20 minute mein khana nahi laaya toh order cancel kar diya aur kitchen ko bol diya 'mat banao'. Agar kitchen phir bhi bana ke le aaye, bill nahi banta -- lekin khana table par aa gaya toh confusion.
how_it_works: Timeout = race(work, timer). Timer jeete toh: abort signal, reject, gate rollback. Work baad mein settle ho toh uska result race ke liye irrelevant. Cancellation cooperative hai, guaranteed nahi.
in_this_project: `test/gates.test.ts` hang test mein `vi.useFakeTimers()`, `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(4999)` aur `(1)`, aur late `resolve()` ke baad snapshot compare. `afterEach` mein `vi.useRealTimers()`.

Boundary (4999 vs 5000 ms) test se fixed
Late answer harmless (lot side par)
disadvantages: Physical side effect ke liye device par bharosa
Timeout chhota ho toh slow-but-working printer bhi fail hoga
common_mistakes: Timeout ke baad bhi late success par confirm kar dena
Real timers se test karna (slow aur flaky)
Signal abort na karna

advanced.failure_scenarios: Device signal ignore kare: barrier timeout ke baad khule, car andar bina reservation (lot ise detect nahi kar sakta). Timeout ke baad device ka late reject: race mein handled, unhandled rejection nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Device se explicit two-step protocol: 'prepare' (print) aur 'commit' (barrier open) -- barrier sirf tab khule jab gate final 'go' bole; ya barrier ke sensor se car ki presence confirm karna.

question: An entry gate reserves a spot and then its process crashes before confirm or cancel. What happens, and how would you fix it?
answer_hinglish:
Imaandari se: yeh project ka documented gap hai. README 'NOT implemented' mein likha hai: 'A reservation whose gate process dies is never cleaned up (there is no expiry sweep); the device timeout covers a hung device, not a crashed gate.'

Kya hota hai: `reserve()` ne spot `reserved` kar diya aur plate `ticketIdByPlate` mein daal di. Timeout `withTimeout` gate ke andar chalta hai -- gate gaya toh timer aur catch bhi gaye. Toh `cancel()` kabhi nahi chalta. Result: woh spot kabhi free nahi hoga, display board ek kam dikhayega, aur us plate wali car kisi bhi gate par ALREADY_PARKED payegi.

Subtle point: is project mein lot aur gates ek hi Node process mein hain, toh 'process crash' ka matlab lot bhi gaya -- sab memory ke saath saaf. Yeh bug realistically tab aata hai jab gate alag process/device ho aur lot ek service ho (ya ek gate ka logic beech mein kisi bug se abandon ho). Toh fix ka design multi-process duniya ke liye hai.

Fix: reservation ko lease banao. Ticket mein `entryAt` already reserve time hai. Ek `expireReservations(maxAgeMs)` jo saare `reserved` entries jinki age maxAge se zyada hai unhe `cancel` kare, timer se chalaya jaaye. Sabse zaroori rule: maxAge gate ke device timeout se clearly bada ho, warna sweep ek zinda gate ka claim cancel kar dega aur uska `confirm` RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND dega jabki barrier khul chuka. Better: gate heartbeat ya lease renew. Yeh sab built nahi hai.
why_needed: Har claim-based system (seat hold, cart inventory hold, distributed lock) ka sawaal: holder mar gaya toh claim kaun chhodega? Bina expiry ke claims resource leak hain.
real_world_analogy: Library book 'hold' par rakhi aur member gayab. Agar hold ki expiry date nahi, toh book shelf par kabhi wapas nahi aayegi.
how_it_works: Claim owner-driven release (confirm/cancel) + time-driven release (lease expiry) -- dono chahiye. Time-driven release ke liye clock aur ek sweeper, aur late owner ke liye clear error.
in_this_project: `src/parking-lot.ts` `reserve` (entryAt = clock.now()), `reservation()` guard jo late confirm ko RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND dega. `statusOf` aur `snapshot` se atke reservations dikh sakte hain. Sweep ka code is project mein nahi hai.

Late confirm ko clear error milta hai
disadvantages: Galat maxAge zinda gate ko tod deta hai
Sweep ka timer aur ek aur moving part
common_mistakes: Device timeout ko crash protection samajhna
Sweep maxAge ko device timeout ke barabar rakhna
Expired reservation ko chupchaap confirm hone dena

Heartbeat vs fixed lease -- kya chunoge?
Barrier khul chuka aur reservation expire ho gaya -- us car ka kya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fixed lease: simple, lekin slow gate ko galat kaat sakta hai. Heartbeat/renewal: precise, lekin gate ko periodic call karna padega. Fencing token (version number) late owner ko galat state likhne se rokta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Sweep aur confirm same tick mein: synchronous methods ki wajah se ek pehle chalega; doosra RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND. Sweep khud crash: lot ke saath hi gaya (in-memory). Clock peeche jaaye: age negative, kuch expire nahi -- safe direction.
advanced.alternatives: Gate ke restart par apne purane reservations cancel karna (gate id store karna padega -- abhi ticket mein gate id nahi hai); database TTL; attendant ke liye manual 'release spot' action.

question: At the exit, the barrier motor fails after beginExit. What state is the car and the ticket in, and can the driver try again?
answer_hinglish:
`ExitGate.leave` mein `beginExit` ne ticket ko `exiting` kar diya aur fee fix kar di. Phir (agar kuch due hai aur card reader hai) payment, phir `await withTimeout(device.open(...))`. Barrier fail hua -- reject ya timeout -- toh catch: `this.lot.abortExit(ticketId)`. `abortExit` sirf status ko `active` karta hai aur lock delete karta hai. Spot `occupied` hi rehta hai, entry waise hi. Phir error: agar cause `ParkingError` hai (PAYMENT_REQUIRED/DECLINED/UNKNOWN) toh wahi rethrow, warna DEVICE_FAILED 'the ticket is still valid'.

Test 'barrier failure: the car is still inside and the ticket works again': device reject 'barrier stuck', p DEVICE_FAILED, `statusOf` `active`, spot `occupied`. Phir ek working device ke saath naya `ExitGate` -- `leave` succeed, ticket gone. Haan, driver dobara try kar sakta hai.

Paise ka case: agar gate ne pehle charge kiya aur `recordPayment` ho gaya, phir barrier fail -- `abortExit` payments ko nahi chhoota (comment: 'Payments recorded during the exit stay recorded'). Agla try exit window ke andar ho toh kuch due nahi, doosra charge nahi. README: 'tested: one charge across both tries'; mutation P11 ('abortExit drops recorded payments') 6 tests se pakdi gayi.

Mutation S3 ('exit gate does not abort on device failure') stage 2 par sirf 1 test se pakdi gayi -- isi test se -- aur stage 3 re-run mein 4 se. Bina abort ke ticket `exiting` mein atak jaata: har agla try TICKET_BUSY, car andar phas jaati.

Limitation: agar barrier sach mein khul gaya lekin device ne error bola, lot kehta hai car andar hai. Ticket phir bhi valid hai -- koi copy le kar nikal sakta hai. Sensor-based confirmation project mein nahi hai.
why_needed: Exit failure par do ulte risks hain: car andar phas jaaye (lock na chhoote) ya double charge ho (payment bhool jaaye). Dono ko design aur tests cover karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Toll plaza par payment ho gaya lekin boom barrier nahi utha. Operator manual entry karta hai 'paid', aur doosri lane par jaane par dobara paisa nahi lagta.
how_it_works: Lock release (status `active`, lock delete) aur payment record alag cheezein hain. Rollback sirf lock ka hota hai, recorded payment fact hai jo rehta hai. Exit window us payment ke time se ginti hai.
in_this_project: `src/gates.ts` `ExitGate.leave` ka catch, `src/parking-lot.ts` `abortExit`. `test/gates.test.ts` barrier failure test; `money.test.ts` mein 'paid then barrier failed -> no second charge'.

Payment record bachta hai, double charge nahi
Payment errors apne code ke saath caller tak
disadvantages: Barrier ka asli physical state lot nahi jaanta
Exit window ke baad dobara try par extra time ka charge (design ke hisaab se sahi, lekin customer ko surprise)
common_mistakes: Abort mein payments bhi reset kar dena
Har error ko DEVICE_FAILED bana dena (mutation P20)
Barrier fail par spot free kar dena
follow_up_questions: Agar abortExit khud throw kare toh?
Barrier sensor ho toh design kaise badlega?
Exit window ke baad retry par kitna charge hoga?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Lock aur payment ko alag rakhna: rollback simple aur double charge se safe. Alternative 'sab ek transaction' tab possible nahi jab beech mein ek external provider hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Barrier khula lekin error: car bahar, lot ke hisaab se andar -- spot kabhi free nahi hoga jab tak koi us ticket se phir exit na kare. Abort ke baad doosra gate turant same ticket le: allowed, kyunki status `active`.
advanced.alternatives: Barrier ke liye retry gate ke andar (ek do baar) before abort; exit ke baad loop sensor se car-gone event aur tab commit.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Multi-gate scale par same; multi-process mein abort ek DB UPDATE (status exiting -> active) aur payment ek alag table insert.
advanced.production_improvements: Barrier failures ka per-gate metric, 'exiting' state mein bahut der tak rehne wale tickets ka alert (crashed exit gate), attendant ke liye override action.

question: Mutation S1 turned EntryGate back into 'check, await the device, then act'. How would you notice this bug in tests or in production, and how do you find and fix it?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: lot almost full hone par do gates par ek saath gaadiyan -- dono ko ticket mil jaata hai, dono barriers khulte hain, phir ek gate ka park LOT_FULL se fail hota hai. Production mein yeh 'car andar hai lekin system mein koi ticket nahi' ya 'device calls zyada, tickets kam' jaisa dikhega. Normal load par chupa rehta hai, sirf peak par.

Tests mein: README ke hisaab se S1 stage 2 par 9 tests fail karta hai (stage 3 re-run mein bhi 9). Kaunse -- README sirf count deta hai, lekin logic se: 'two gates, one free spot: only one ticket is printed' (device calls 1 ki jagah 2), 'the same plate at two gates' (ALREADY_PARKED device ke baad aata), 'while the device runs, the spot is reserved' (spot abhi bhi `free`), aur random concurrent-gates test ke seeds, jahan invariant 'every pending device call is backed by a claim' turant toot jaata hai -- pending entry call ka `statusOf` undefined.

Investigation: invariant failure message batata hai ek device call bina `reserved` status ke chal raha hai. Phir `EntryGate.enter` dekho -- kya `lot.reserve()` await se PEHLE hai? Naive version mein check `availability()` se hai aur act (`park`) await ke baad. Wahi pattern jo test file ke `NaiveEntryGate` mein documented hai.

Fix: claim pehle, synchronously (`reserve`), device await baad mein, phir `confirm`, aur catch mein `cancel`. Kyun kaam karta hai: check aur change ek synchronous call mein -- beech mein koi doosra gate nahi aa sakta. Lesson: yeh bug ek line move karne jitna chhota hai, isliye 9 tests ka safety net zaroori hai.
why_needed: Check-then-act sabse common concurrency bug hai aur code review mein 'theek' dikhta hai. Usko symptom se pehchaanna interview ka core skill hai.
real_world_analogy: Do cashier ek hi 'last item' bech dete hain kyunki dono ne shelf dekha, phir billing ki, phir item uthane gaye.
how_it_works: Mutation testing: ek deliberate bug daalo, poora suite chalao, dekho kitne tests fail. 0 fail = test gap. S1 ke 9 failures batate hain ki is bug ko kai angles se pakda jaata hai.
in_this_project: README 'Mutation checks' table: S1 'entry gate checks, awaits the device, then acts (the naive gate)' -- 9 failed. Runner scripts repo ke bahar rakhe gaye hain (README). Naive gate ka reference implementation `test/gates.test.ts` mein `NaiveEntryGate`.

Invariant failure seedha cause ki taraf point karta hai
disadvantages: Production mein sirf load par dikhta hai
Bina controllable fake device ke reproduce karna mushkil
common_mistakes: Flaky failure ko 'timing issue' bol ke retry lagana
Fix mein sleep/delay daalna
Sirf LOT_FULL ka error message improve karna

Kya ek test kaafi tha? 9 kyun acche hain?
Mutation testing ko CI mein kaise chalaoge?

question: Mutations S2 and S3 removed the rollback when a gate's device fails. What would the symptom be in a running lot, and how do you trace it back?
answer_hinglish:
S2: entry gate device fail par `cancel` nahi karta. S3: exit gate device fail par `abortExit` nahi karta. Dono mein gate DEVICE_FAILED throw toh karta hai -- caller ko sab theek lagta hai -- lekin claim atka reh jaata hai.

S2 ka symptom: har printer jam ek spot kha jaata hai. Spot `reserved` mein, plate map mein. Display board free count kam dikhata hai, aur jam ke baad wahi driver dobara try kare toh ALREADY_PARKED -- 'main toh andar gaya hi nahi!' Din bhar mein lot 'full' dikhne lagta hai jabki spots khaali hain. S3 ka symptom: barrier fail ke baad ticket `exiting` mein atka -- har agla try TICKET_BUSY, car andar phas gayi, sirf restart se theek.

Investigation: (1) `snapshot()` dekho -- kitne spots `reserved` hain aur unke `heldBy` ka `statusOf` kya hai; koi physical car nahi lekin reserved = leaked claim. (2) Exit side par `statusOf(ticket)` `exiting` aur koi gate us par kaam nahi kar raha. (3) Logs mein DEVICE_FAILED ke saath ticket id correlate karo -- har leaked claim ek DEVICE_FAILED ke baad. (4) Phir gate ke catch block mein dekho rollback call hai ya nahi.

Tests: README ke hisaab se S2 stage 2 par 3 tests se, stage 3 re-run mein 4 se. S3 stage 2 par sirf 1 test se pakdi -- README use 'caught by exactly one test' list mein rakhta hai, matlab woh test ('barrier failure: the car is still inside and the ticket works again') delete hua toh bug chhup jaata. Stage 3 mein 4 tests.

Fix: har claim ke saath try/catch jahan catch pehle rollback, phir throw. Kyun: claim ka har exit path terminal state mein jaana chahiye.
why_needed: Missing rollback 'slow leak' bug hai -- crash nahi, error bhi sahi, lekin resource dheere dheere khatam. Aise bugs production mein der se pakde jaate hain.
real_world_analogy: Hotel jahan check-in fail hone par room 'hold' se hataaya hi nahi jaata. Hafte bhar mein reception 'house full' bolti hai jabki aadhe kamre khaali.
how_it_works: Leak detection = state ka cross-check: claim exist karta hai lekin koi owner usko process nahi kar raha. Is lot mein owner ka koi record nahi (gate id store nahi hoti), isliye correlation logs ya age se hoti hai.
in_this_project: Tests: 'device failure: DEVICE_FAILED with the cause, reservation cancelled, spot and plate free again', 'a device that throws synchronously...', 'a device that hangs...' (entry) aur 'barrier failure...' (exit) in `test/gates.test.ts`; random concurrent test bhi -- leaked reservation ki wajah se 'pending call backed by claim' aur device-call counts ki assertions.
advantages: Bug ka exact location (catch block) chhota hai
snapshot/statusOf se state inspect ho jaata hai
disadvantages: Lot mein claim ki age ya gate id nahi, toh 'kitna purana' direct nahi dikhta
S3 sirf ek test par tiki thi (stage 2)
common_mistakes: DEVICE_FAILED ko 'sirf hardware problem' maan kar ignore karna
Restart se 'theek' karke root cause na dhoondhna
finally mein rollback daal dena (success par bhi cancel ho jaata)
follow_up_questions: Ek test par tiki mutation ko kaise strong karoge?
Claim leak ke liye kaunsa metric banaoge?
Rollback khud fail ho toh kya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Rollback gate mein (abhi) vs lot mein (lease) -- gate wala fast aur exact, lease wala crash-safe lekin approximate. Dono saath best.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Rollback call khud throw kare (bookkeeping bug -> SPOT_STATE): original device error kho sakta hai. Gate crash: catch chalta hi nahi -- wahi known gap.
advanced.alternatives: Lot mein claim ke saath `claimedAt` aur gate id rakhna taaki leak query se dikhe; RAII-style helper jo claim object return kare aur `using`/finally se release kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Ek gate par roz 1% jams bhi bade lot mein kuch ghanton mein saare spots kha sakte hain -- isliye leak ka impact traffic ke saath badhta hai.

question: Mutations S5, S6 and S7 each broke withTimeout in a different way and each was caught by only one test. What does each bug look like in production?
answer_hinglish:
Teeno `src/timeout.ts` ke andar ki galtiyan hain, aur README stage 2 par teeno ko 'caught by exactly one test' list mein rakhta hai (stage 3 re-run mein bhi har ek 1).

S5 -- timeout signal abort nahi karta. Gate timeout ke baad reservation cancel kar deta hai, lekin device ko kabhi pata nahi chalta. Production symptom: printer der se jaagta hai, ticket print karta hai, barrier kholta hai -- car andar aati hai jabki uska spot free ho chuka aur kisi aur ko mil sakta hai. Logs mein DEVICE_FAILED, phir bhi camera mein car. Pakadne wala test: hang test ka `device.calls[0].signal.aborted` true assertion.

S6 -- fast device ke baad timer clear nahi hota. Functionally sab sahi, lekin har call ek 10 s timer chhodta hai jo baad mein `abort()` aur reject chalata hai (koi sunne wala nahi). Symptom: process graceful shutdown mein 10 s atakta hai, test runs slow, aur bahut traffic par hazaron pending timers. Test: 'a fast device clears its timer' -- `vi.getTimerCount()` 0.

S7 -- race hi nahi, seedha work ka await. Hung device = gate ka `enter` kabhi settle nahi hota, reservation hamesha atka, aur caller (UI) bhi hamesha wait karta. Symptom: ek gate 'freeze', ek spot permanently reserved. Test: hang test -- reasoning se, fake timer advance hone ke baad bhi DEVICE_FAILED nahi aata.

Investigation tools: S6 ke liye `process._getActiveHandles()`/why-is-node-running jaisa tool; S5/S7 ke liye per-gate device latency aur 'timeout count' metrics. Lesson: har ek property (abort, clear, race) ka apna dedicated assertion hai, aur woh ek test delete hua toh bug chhup jaata.
why_needed: Timeout code chhota hota hai lekin teen alag guarantees deta hai. Har guarantee ka apna symptom samajhna 'it works' se aage ka debugging skill hai.
real_world_analogy: Alarm clock: S5 = alarm bajta hai lekin aap jaagte nahi; S6 = subah uthne ke baad bhi alarm set rehta hai aur dopahar mein baj jaata hai; S7 = alarm laga hi nahi.
how_it_works: withTimeout ki teen properties: (1) deadline par abort signal, (2) jo bhi jeete timer clear, (3) race se caller bounded time mein settle. Har ek ko alag observable se test kiya: `signal.aborted`, `getTimerCount()`, aur fake time par settle hona.
in_this_project: `src/timeout.ts` `withTimeout`; `test/gates.test.ts` ke do fake-timer tests. README stage 2 table: S5 1, S6 1, S7 1.
advantages: Har property ka precise observable
Fake timers se tests fast aur deterministic
disadvantages: Har bug sirf ek test par tiki -- woh test fragile ho ya delete ho toh coverage gayi
S5 ka asli nuksaan device behaviour par depend, jo test ka fake simulate karta hai
common_mistakes: Timer leak ko 'harmless' maanna
Timeout test real 10 s wait karke likhna
Abort ko optional maanna 'kyunki gate already cancel karta hai'
follow_up_questions: Ek-test-wali mutations ke liye doosra test kaise likhoge?
Production mein timer leak kaise detect karoge?
AbortSignal.timeout + AbortSignal.any se yeh function kaise simple hoga?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Apna withTimeout likhna vs Node built-ins (`AbortSignal.timeout`): apne mein control aur clear semantics, built-in mein kam code lekin late-answer aur timer cleanup ka behaviour samajhna padta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: S5: physical side effect after rollback (sabse khatarnak). S6: resource leak, shutdown delay. S7: liveness failure, claim forever.
advanced.alternatives: Ek generic `withDeadline` library; ya device driver khud apna timeout lagaye -- lekin tab gate ko driver par bharosa karna padta.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: S6 ka impact traffic ke saath linear: har device call ek leaked timer, 10 s tak. 100x traffic par memory aur event-loop timers badhte hain.
advanced.production_improvements: Har property ke liye doosra independent test (jaise random concurrent test mein timer count check), shutdown par active handles check, timeout aur late-answer metrics.

question: Two cars drove out on one ticket. Which mutations in the README produce that bug, and how do you narrow down where the lock was lost?
answer_hinglish:
Ek ticket par do exits ka matlab do exit gates dono `beginExit` -> device tak pahunch gaye. README mein yeh bug kai roop mein toda gaya:

- S4 'exit gate without the lock (quote, await, exit)' -- naive exit gate; stage 2 par 16 tests fail.
- S17 'beginExit does not lock the ticket' -- gate theek, lekin lot status `exiting` set nahi karta; 28 tests fail. (Stage 3 par S4 aur S17 'no longer apply as written' kyunki exit gate aur lock rewrite hue.)
- S18 'no TICKET_BUSY check' -- lock set hota hai lekin `unlocked()` guard check nahi karta; stage 2 par 7, stage 3 par 9.
- Stage 3 ka P13 'beginPayment / beginExit do not lock the ticket' -- 47 tests.

Narrow karne ka tareeka -- teen jagah, upar se neeche: (1) Gate: `ExitGate.leave` mein kya `beginExit` device se PEHLE hai? Agar `quote()` se check hai toh S4. (2) Lot ka lock: `beginExit` ke baad `statusOf(ticket)` `exiting` hai? Nahi toh S17/P13 type (`lockEntry` nahi chala). (3) Guard: status `exiting` hai, phir bhi doosra `beginExit` pass? Toh `unlocked()` ka check gayab -- S18.

Fastest test: `two-phase.test.ts` ka 'beginExit fixes the fee and locks the ticket' -- `beginExit` ke baad `statusOf` `exiting`, doosra `beginExit` TICKET_BUSY. Aur gate level par 'one ticket at two exit gates' (`device.calls` 1, gateway total 5000). Production mein symptom: ek ticket id ke do barrier-open events, ya provider ke paas ek ticket ke do charges.

Fix: lock synchronously, guard har entry point par, aur gate hamesha lock pehle le.
why_needed: Ek hi symptom ke kai causes ho sakte hain; layered narrowing (gate -> lock -> guard) debugging time bachata hai.
real_world_analogy: Gate pass do baar use hua: ya guard ne dekha hi nahi (S4), ya register mein 'in use' likha hi nahi (S17), ya likha par guard ne padha nahi (S18).
how_it_works: Lock ke teen hisse: lena (status set), dekhna (guard), aur sahi order mein use karna (gate). Teeno mein se koi bhi toote toh same symptom. Har layer ko alag observable se verify karo.
in_this_project: `src/parking-lot.ts` `beginExit`, `lockEntry`, `unlocked`; `src/gates.ts` `ExitGate.leave`. Mutation counts sab README ke stage 2/stage 3 tables se.

Bade mutation counts (16, 28, 47) dikhate hain coverage gehri hai

question: Coding exercise: add a reservation expiry sweep to ParkingLot (expireReservations(maxAgeMs)) and a test that proves it, without breaking the gate's safety.
answer_hinglish:
Yeh feature project mein NAHI hai -- README ka known gap hai ('A reservation whose gate process dies is never cleaned up'). Exercise ka solution neeche hai.

Design: `expireReservations(maxAgeMs)` synchronous lot method. `this.clock.now()` lo, saare entries mein se jinka status `reserved` hai aur `now - ticket.entryAt > maxAgeMs` -- unke ids pehle ek array mein collect karo, phir har ek par existing `cancel()` call karo. Existing `cancel` reuse karne se spot release, index push, plate delete aur board event sab apne aap -- koi naya rollback logic nahi. Return: expire kiye ids (logging ke liye).

Pehle collect, phir cancel kyun: `cancel` -> `forget` -> `changeFree` -> listeners synchronously chalte hain, aur koi listener lot ko change kar sakta hai. Map ko iterate karte hue mutate karna risky hai. Isliye har cancel se pehle dobara check karo ki status abhi bhi `reserved` hai.

Safety rule: `maxAgeMs` gate ke device timeout (default 10 s) se clearly bada hona chahiye. Warna sweep ek zinda gate ka claim cancel kar dega; gate ka baad mein `confirm` RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND phenkega -- lekin barrier khul chuka hoga. Isliye constructor mein validation ya documentation.

Test: `ManualClock` se time control. Do reservations -- ek purani (gate 'crashed'), ek nayi. Time aage, sweep, assert: purani gone, nayi `reserved`, free count sahi, wahi plate aur spot phir se reserve ho sakte hain, aur purane id par late `confirm` RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND.
why_needed: Claim-based design ka natural next step yahi hai, aur interviewer aksar 'crashed gate ka kya?' poochta hai -- code se jawab dena strong signal hai.
real_world_analogy: Library ka 'hold shelf': har din librarian dekhta hai kaunsi books 3 din se zyada hold par hain aur unhe wapas shelf par rakhti hai.
how_it_works: Time-based release existing owner-based release (`cancel`) ko reuse karta hai. Synchronous method hone se sweep aur gate ka confirm interleave nahi hote -- ek pehle, ek baad. Late owner ko `reservation()` guard clear error deta hai.
in_this_project: Reuse hone wale existing pieces: `cancel`, `reservation` guard, `ticket.entryAt` (reserve time), `ManualClock.advance`, `statusOf`, `availability`. Naya code sirf sweep method aur test hai (dono illustrative, repo mein nahi).
advantages: Existing cancel reuse -- index, plate, board sab consistent
Synchronous, toh gate ke confirm se race nahi
Test pure ManualClock se, koi real wait nahi
disadvantages: O(entries) scan har sweep par
Galat maxAge zinda gate ko tod deta hai
Sweep ko koi timer se chalana padega (lot khud timer nahi rakhta)
common_mistakes: Iterate karte hue Map se delete karna bina snapshot ke
Spot ko seedha free karna aur plate/index/board bhool jaana
maxAge ko device timeout ke barabar rakhna

Barrier khul chuka aur reservation expire ho gaya toh us car ka kya?
Invariants test mein sweep ko kaise add karoge?

advanced.failure_scenarios: Sweep listener ko trigger karta hai jo throw kare: EventQueue pakadta hai. Clock peeche jaaye: age negative, kuch expire nahi. Gate ka late confirm: RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND -- gate ko yeh case handle karna padega (log + attendant alert).
advanced.alternatives: Per-reservation `setTimeout` (har reserve par ek timer -- bahut saare timers, aur cleanup ki zimmedari); heartbeat/lease renewal; DB-level TTL.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade lot mein `reserved` entries ka alag min-heap by entryAt -- sweep O(expired x log n). Multi-process mein ek SQL UPDATE with WHERE reserved_at < cutoff.

question: Coding exercise: write a test that reproduces the exit race with a naive gate and then proves the real ExitGate opens only one barrier for a copied ticket.
answer_hinglish:
Idea: same setup do baar -- pehle naive exit gate se bug dikhao (do barriers), phir real `ExitGate` se fix (ek barrier, doosra TICKET_BUSY). Interleaving test control kare, isliye `FakeDevice` use karo jiske calls pending rehte hain jab tak test resolve na kare.

Steps: (1) ek compact spot wala lot, car park karo. Time aage nahi badhaya, toh stay grace ke andar hai aur kuch due nahi -- card reader ki zaroorat nahi. (2) Naive: do `NaiveExitGate.leave(t.id)` bina await, `flush()`, assert `device.calls` length 2 -- bug. Dono resolve, `allSettled`: ek fulfilled, ek rejected (barrier ke baad). (3) Naya lot, real: do `ExitGate.leave(t.id)`. Doosra turant TICKET_BUSY se reject -- `beginExit` ka lock. `flush()`, assert `device.calls` length 1. Resolve, `await p1`, ticket gone (`statusOf` undefined).

Dhyaan: `p2` ko pehle `expect(...).rejects` se handle karo, warna unhandled rejection warning. Aur `device.calls` ka count hi asli assertion hai -- final state dono cases mein same dikhta hai (ticket gone), farak sirf physical side effect (barrier kitni baar khula) mein hai.

Yeh test basically `gates.test.ts` ke do existing tests ka combination hai; repo mein naive aur real exit tests alag-alag describe blocks mein hain. Exercise ka point yeh dikhana hai ki ek test bug aur fix ko side by side document kare.
why_needed: Concurrency fix ka proof sirf 'mere fix ke saath test pass' nahi hai -- pehle bug reproduce karna padta hai, warna pata nahi test kuch check bhi kar raha hai.
real_world_analogy: Doctor pehle bimari ka test positive dikhata hai, phir dawai ke baad negative -- sirf 'negative' report ka matlab kuch nahi agar test kabhi positive aa hi nahi sakta.
how_it_works: Pending-promise fake device + `setImmediate` flush = test interleaving decide karta hai. Assertion side effect count par, state par nahi.
in_this_project: Reuse: `test/gates.test.ts` ke `makeLot`, `FakeDevice`, `NaiveExitGate`, `flush`. Real gate bina gateway ke kaam karta hai kyunki `quote.dueMinor` 0 hai (wahi jaise 'barrier failure' test mein).
