Deterministic, koi timers nahi
disadvantages: Naive gate test file mein duplicate code hai jo library ke saath sync nahi rehta
Ek test mein do scenarios -- fail hone par message kam specific
common_mistakes: Sirf final state assert karna (dono mein ticket gone)
p2 ki rejection handle na karna
Real timers aur sleep se interleaving banana
follow_up_questions: Due amount ho toh is test mein kya badlega?
Isko pay station + exit gate race ke liye kaise badloge?
Do describe blocks vs ek test -- kya behtar hai?

question: AbortSignal does not kill a promise. What does cooperative cancellation mean for the gate devices, and what exactly does this project guarantee versus rely on?
answer_hinglish:
JavaScript mein koi promise ko bahar se 'kill' nahi kar sakta. `controller.abort()` sirf `signal.aborted` ko true karta hai aur `abort` event fire karta hai. Jo code signal sunta hai woh khud ruk sakta hai -- `fetch` jaisa built-in rukta hai, lekin ek custom device driver tabhi rukega jab usne signal check kiya ho. Isko cooperative cancellation kehte hain.

Project kya GUARANTEE karta hai: (1) timeout par signal abort hota hai (test: `signal.aborted` true); (2) gate ka claim rollback hota hai -- reservation cancel ya exit abort; (3) late answer lot ka state nahi badalta -- race settle ho chuka, `confirm`/`commitExit` nahi chalte; (4) timer clear hota hai. Yeh sab lot ke logical state ke baare mein hai.

Project kya RELY karta hai: device signal dekh ke physical action roke -- barrier na khole. README 'NOT implemented' mein clearly: 'The device must honour the AbortSignal (not open the barrier after a timeout); the fakes in the tests do, real hardware is not part of this project.' `EntryDevice` interface ke comment mein bhi: 'a real device driver must stop, e.g. not open the barrier, when it is.'

Kyun yeh important hai: timeout ke baad lot ne spot free kar diya. Agar barrier baad mein khul jaaye, toh car andar aur doosri car ko wahi spot -- original bug, bas timeout ke raaste se. Isliye real system mein driver ko signal check karna chahiye barrier motor chalane se pehle, aur ideally hardware level par bhi 'open only if command still valid'. Saath hi ek aur gap: agar barrier motor already chal raha hai aur tab abort aaye, toh rok nahi sakte -- tab sensor se reality pata karni padegi.
why_needed: Cancellation ke baare mein galat assumption ('timeout ke baad kaam ruk gaya') distributed systems mein double-processing aur ghost side effects ka common cause hai.
real_world_analogy: Waiter ko bola 'order cancel'. Ab yeh kitchen par hai ki woh sun ke chulha band kare. Agar kitchen ne nahi suna, toh khana banega -- aapke 'cancel' bolne se pan nahi rukta.
how_it_works: AbortController -> AbortSignal (aborted flag + 'abort' event + reason). Consumer ya toh `signal.aborted` poll kare, ya `signal.addEventListener('abort', ...)`, ya signal ko aage built-in APIs ko pass kare. Promise.race sirf caller ko unblock karta hai, worker ko nahi.
in_this_project: `src/gates.ts` mein `EntryDevice.issue(ticket, signal)` aur `ExitDevice.open(quote, signal)` -- signal interface ka hissa hai, optional nahi. `src/timeout.ts` abort karta hai. Payment gateway bhi signal leta hai (`charge(req, signal)` -- invariants test mein dikhta hai).
advantages: Signal interface mein compulsory hai, toh har driver ko usse deal karna padta hai
Lot ka logical state device ke behaviour se independent safe
disadvantages: Physical safety driver ki discipline par
Point of no return ke baad abort bekaar
common_mistakes: Sochna `abort()` promise reject/stop kar deta hai
Signal ko interface mein optional rakhna
Driver mein barrier kholne se pehle signal check na karna
follow_up_questions: Barrier motor chalne ke baad abort aaye toh?
AbortSignal.reason kya hai aur kyun useful hai?
Payment gateway mein cancellation aur idempotency kaise saath kaam karte hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Cooperative cancellation simple aur portable hai lekin guarantee nahi deta. Hard guarantee ke liye hardware/protocol level par 'commit token' chahiye -- zyada complex.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Driver signal ignore: ghost barrier open. Signal check aur barrier open ke beech abort: race window chhoti lekin exist karti hai. Late reject: Promise.race handle karta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Two-phase device protocol (prepare/commit), barrier controller jo gate se short-lived token maange, ya sensor-based reconciliation.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada gates par same; har gate ka apna controller. Network-connected devices par latency badhti hai, toh timeout aur race window dono par sochna padta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Driver contract tests (har driver ko ek test suite pass karna ho jo aborted signal par barrier na khule), late-answer logging, aur sensor events se reconciliation.

question: Your lot's state and the physical world can disagree: the barrier opened but the device reported failure, or it timed out after opening. How would you reason about and close that gap?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: is project mein lot ka state device ki REPORT par chalta hai, reality par nahi. Device bola 'fail' toh lot maanta hai kuch nahi hua -- entry par reservation cancel, exit par `abortExit`. Yeh tab tak sahi hai jab tak device sach bole aur signal honour kare (README ki shart). Real duniya mein do mismatch ho sakte hain:

1. Entry: barrier khula, phir device ne error/timeout diya. Lot: spot free, plate free. Reality: car andar bina ticket. Agla car ussi spot ke liye ticket pa sakta hai.
2. Exit: barrier khula, car nikli, device ne error diya. Lot: ticket `active`, spot `occupied`. Reality: spot khaali. Spot kabhi free nahi hoga jab tak koi us ticket se phir exit na kare -- aur ticket valid hai, toh copy wala bhi nikal sakta hai.

Yeh distributed systems ka classic 'unknown outcome' problem hai -- wahi jo payment mein PAYMENT_UNKNOWN hai (charge hua ya nahi pata nahi). Payment ke liye project idempotency key aur 'unknown' code use karta hai; devices ke liye aisa kuch nahi bana.

Close karne ke tareeke (koi bhi built nahi): (a) device result ko teen-valued banao: ok / failed-before-action / unknown. Unknown par claim rollback mat karo, 'needs attention' state mein rakho. (b) Barrier par sensors (loop detector, camera) aur ek reconciliation job jo lot state ko occupancy sensors se milaye. (c) Device protocol mein point of no return ke baad ka failure alag report ho. (d) Attendant ke liye manual override ops. Principle: jab outcome unknown ho, toh confident 'failed' mat bolo -- PLAN.md payment ke liye yahi kehta hai: outcome 'reported as unknown, not as failed, because it may have succeeded'.
why_needed: LLD rounds mein 'happy path + rollback' sab likhte hain; senior signal yeh hai ki aap pehchano rollback khud galat ho sakta hai jab outcome unknown ho.
real_world_analogy: Courier company ka tracking: delivery boy bola 'deliver nahi hua', lekin parcel darwaze par pada hai. System ko proof-of-delivery photo (sensor) chahiye, sirf boy ki report nahi.
how_it_works: Exactly-once side effects network/hardware boundary ke paar possible nahi; at-least-once ya at-most-once + reconciliation hi practical hai. Unknown outcome ke liye ek explicit state chahiye, binary success/fail se kaam nahi chalta.
in_this_project: Abhi: `EntryGate` har device error par `cancel`, `ExitGate` par `abortExit`. Payment side par is pattern ka ulta example hai -- `PAYMENT_UNKNOWN` aur same idempotency key se retry, aur README kehta hai reconciliation built nahi. Devices ke liye unknown state ya sensors ka koi model nahi.
advantages: Abhi ka model simple aur testable hai
Payment side ka unknown-outcome pattern devices par bhi lagaya ja sakta hai
disadvantages: Lot reality se drift kar sakta hai aur khud detect nahi kar sakta
Exit mismatch par valid ticket ek security hole ban jaata hai
common_mistakes: Device report ko ground truth maanna
Unknown outcome ko 'failed' bol kar rollback karna
Reconciliation ko 'baad mein dekh lenge' chhod dena
follow_up_questions: Barrier sensors ke saath state machine kaise badlegi?
Kis case mein rollback karna galat hai?
Payment ka PAYMENT_UNKNOWN aur device ka unknown -- ek design mein kaise laoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Binary success/fail: simple code, lekin unknown ko galat side par daal deta hai. Teen-valued result: zyada states aur human workflow, lekin reality ke kareeb. Fail-safe direction chunna padega -- entry par 'spot reserved rakho' (ek spot waste) vs 'free karo' (double allocation risk).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Sensor bhi fail ho sakta hai; reconciliation job lag kare toh window mein galat allocation; human override galat bhi ho sakta hai -- audit log chahiye.
advanced.alternatives: Barrier controller jo khud lot service se 'commit' le (device local decision na kare); occupancy sensors per spot jo spot state ka source of truth ban jaayein; camera-based plate read entry/exit par.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare lots par reconciliation ek central job jo sensor events aur ticket events stream se compare kare (event sourcing style) -- built nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-spot occupancy sensors, 'unknown' device results ka queue attendant UI mein, daily reconciliation report, aur device events ka audit log ticket id ke saath.

question: Why are EntryGate and ExitGate separate classes from ParkingLot instead of async methods on the lot itself?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki dono ke kaam ki nature alag hai. `ParkingLot` rules aur state ka owner hai -- har method synchronous, 'check everything, then change', aur yahi synchronous hona concurrency ki safety deta hai. Gates slow, failure-prone duniya se baat karte hain: printer, barrier, card reader -- sab async, timeout wale, fail hone wale.

Agar lot par `async enterWithDevice()` hota, toh lot ke andar await aa jaata -- aur woh exactly woh jagah hai jahan race ghusti hai. Alag classes se boundary saaf hai: lot ke andar koi await nahi, gate sirf do lot calls ke BEECH mein await karta hai. Har gate ka pattern: claim (`reserve`/`beginExit`), slow kaam, commit (`confirm`/`commitExit`) ya rollback (`cancel`/`abortExit`).

Doosre fayde: (1) Devices interfaces hain (`EntryDevice`, `ExitDevice`) jo constructor mein inject hote hain -- tests `FakeDevice` dete hain, production real driver. (2) Har gate ka apna config: `timeoutMs`, aur `ExitGate` ke liye optional `gateway` (card reader) aur retry options. (3) Lot ko bina gates ke bhi use kar sakte ho: `park()` (reserve + confirm) aur `exit()` (attendant booth, cash) synchronous one-step versions hain. (4) `PayStation` bhi same shape follow karta hai -- ek aur 'async shell' jo lot ke `beginPayment`/`recordPayment`/`abortPayment` use karta hai.

Ek important rule jo boundary se aaya: barrier rule lot mein hai, gate mein nahi -- `commitExit` PAYMENT_REQUIRED deta hai agar kuch due hai, toh buggy gate bhi unpaid car ko nahi nikaal sakta (mutation P24).
why_needed: Synchronous core + async shell ek reusable architecture hai: business rules testable aur race-free, IO ka mess bahar. Interviewer responsibility split dekhna chahta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka core ledger (sirf entries, turant, rules ke saath) vs ATM machine (cash dispenser, network, jam). ATM ledger ko call karta hai, ledger ATM ka intezaar nahi karta.
how_it_works: Lot = domain core (sync, pure state + rules). Gate = application service/adapter (async orchestration, timeouts, device IO). Dependency direction: gate -> lot, gate -> device interface; lot kisi gate ya device ko nahi jaanta.
in_this_project: `src/gates.ts` mein `EntryGate`, `ExitGate`, `EntryDevice`, `ExitDevice`, `GateOptions`, `ExitGateOptions`. `src/parking-lot.ts` mein koi `async` method nahi. README ka class diagram yahi layering dikhata hai.
advantages: Lot ke andar await ki koi jagah nahi -- race ka raasta band
Devices inject hote hain, tests fake kar sakte hain
Har gate ka alag config
disadvantages: Do layers samajhni padti hain
Rollback ki zimmedari gate par hai -- gate bug kare toh claim leak (S2/S3)
common_mistakes: Lot mein async device calls daalna
Business rules (payment check) gate mein rakhna
Device ko lot ke andar inject karna
follow_up_questions: PayStation aur ExitGate ka same lock kyun?
Gate ko HTTP API ke peeche le jaana ho toh kya badlega?
Barrier rule lot mein kyun, gate mein kyun nahi?

question: Turn this library into a real system: 20 gates with their own controllers talking to a central lot service over a network. What changes in the claim protocol?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest baseline: project ek in-memory library hai, ek Node process, koi HTTP API ya database nahi (PLAN.md 'Not in scope'). Neeche ka design built nahi hai, lekin claim pattern seedha map hota hai.

Architecture: ek lot service jo `ParkingLot` jaisa synchronous core chalaye (ek writer per lot, ya state database mein conditional UPDATE ke saath). Gate controllers network par `reserve`, `confirm`, `cancel`, `beginExit`, `commitExit`, `abortExit` call karein. Device ka slow kaam gate controller par local hi rahe.

Network se teen nayi problems aati hain jo ek process mein nahi thi:

1. Lost response: gate ne `reserve` bheja, service ne spot claim kiya, jawab kho gaya. Gate retry kare toh doosra spot claim -- leak. Fix: gate ek request id bheje; service usi id par wahi ticket return kare (idempotency) -- wahi idea jo project payment ke `paymentKey` mein use karta hai.
2. Gate crash/partition: claim hamesha atka -- project ka known gap ab aur zaroori. Fix: lease (reserved_at + expiry) aur gate heartbeat; expiry gate ke device timeout se lamba.
3. Stale owner: lease expire hua, phir purana gate `confirm` bheje. Project mein yeh RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND hota, jo sahi hai; lekin barrier khul chuka -- tab 'unknown outcome' wala reconciliation chahiye.

Jo SAME rehta hai: claim-slow work-commit/rollback ka shape, error codes (TICKET_BUSY, ALREADY_PARKED, RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND, EXIT_NOT_STARTED caller ke liye already meaningful), barrier rule service mein (commitExit PAYMENT_REQUIRED). Partition mein gate kya kare -- fail closed (entry band) ya offline tickets -- yeh business decision hai.
why_needed: Interviewer LLD ke baad hamesha 'ab isko distributed banao' poochta hai. Achha jawab dikhata hai ki kaunse guarantees network ke paar automatically toot jaate hain aur kaunsa design idea reuse hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek central booking office aur 20 counters phone line par. Phone kat gaya toh counter ko pata nahi booking hui ya nahi -- isliye har request ka ek reference number, aur 'hold' ki expiry.
how_it_works: Ek-process atomicity -> service ke andar single-writer ya DB atomic statements. Function call -> RPC with timeouts, idempotency keys, leases. Crash ab sirf gate ka hota hai, lot ka nahi -- toh orphan claims real problem ban jaate hain.
in_this_project: Reuse hone wale pieces: `ParkingLot` ke synchronous methods (service ke andar), `TicketStatus` states, payment side ka idempotency key pattern (`paymentKey`, `chargeWithRetry` mein same key every retry), aur `withTimeout`. Missing pieces: request ids for reserve, leases, persistence -- README aur PLAN.md dono 'not built' kehte hain.
advantages: Claim pattern network ke paar bhi same rehta hai
Error codes already API-ready
Idempotency pattern payment side se reuse
disadvantages: Har gate operation ab network round trip
Leases, request ids, persistence -- teen naye moving parts
Partition mein availability vs safety ka decision
common_mistakes: Network call ko local function call jaisa treat karna (retry = double reserve)
Lease na rakhna
Lot logic ko gate controllers mein copy karna
follow_up_questions: Partition ke time gate entry de ya na de?
Ek writer per lot vs shared DB -- kab kya?
Reserve ki idempotency key kaun generate kare?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Single-writer lot service (in-memory core + persistence log): fast aur project ke code ke kareeb, lekin failover ka design chahiye. Shared DB with conditional UPDATEs: stateless services, lekin har claim ek DB round trip aur hot rows par contention.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Lost reserve response: duplicate claim (request id se fix). Gate partition: orphan claims (lease se fix). Service down: koi entry/exit nahi -- fail closed ya local fallback. Clock skew gate vs service: lease time service ke clock par hi gino.
advanced.alternatives: Gate controllers par local cache ke saath optimistic entry aur baad mein reconcile (zyada availability, kam safety); event-sourced log of claims; per-lot actor.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x lots: lot_id se shard -- claims kabhi lots cross nahi karte, toh scaling natural. 100x gates per lot: phir bhi ek lot ka critical section chhota; bottleneck network aur DB, logic nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Idempotent reserve API, leases with heartbeat, persistence aur replay, per-gate health metrics, reconciliation with occupancy sensors, aur chaos tests (drop responses, kill gates) jo random concurrent test ka network version hon.
